headline: Accused in 30 cases fled prison van in Dhaka
summary: Pichchi Raja, a criminal accused in 30 cases, escaped while being transported back to Kashimpur Central Jail.
details: Pichchi Raja, a criminal accused in 30 cases, escaped from a prison van in Dhaka’s Tantibazar area while being transported back to Kashimpur Central Jail after a court appearance.

caption:
A criminal accused in 30 cases escaped a prison van in Dhaka, with police alleging the escape was staged by security personnel.

Pichchi Raja, a criminal accused in 30 cases, escaped from a prison van in Dhaka’s Tantibazar area while being transported back to Kashimpur Central Jail after a court appearance.

Initial reports stated the escape occurred near Baimail in Gazipur, but a police investigation revealed the actual location was near the Popular Diagnostic Centre in Tantibazar.

Investigators believe Raja fled in a waiting private car after being let out of the vehicle by escort team leader SI Prabir Biswas.

Police allege that the account of Raja escaping while using a toilet near Baimail was staged by the security personnel involved.

Following the investigation, police arrested SI Prabir Kumar, driver Kamal Hossain, and Raja’s sister, Taslima.

Sub-inspector Prabir Kumar, along with constables Md Zakir Hossain, Md Sakib, and Shakil Hossain, and driver Kamal Hossain, have been suspended for alleged negligence.

headline_marked: 2 [[Indian nationals shot by BSF]] after being mistaken for Bangladeshis
headline: 2 Indian nationals shot by BSF after being mistaken for Bangladeshis
summary: The victims, residents of Assam, were allegedly beaten and shot by the BSF on the Indian side of the border in Kurigram.
details: Two Indian citizens from the South Salmara Mancachar district of Assam were shot by the Border Security Force (BSF) on Sunday night in the Ulipur border area of Kurigram.
The victims, identified as mason Ismail Hossain and Abdul Alim, were allegedly detained by BSF members inside Indian territory during a cattle smuggling operation.
Ismail Hossain reported that BSF personnel beat him with sticks and shot him after mistakenly claiming he was a Bangladeshi, despite his pleas that he was an Indian citizen.
The BSF allegedly left the victims bleeding at the zero line of the Bangladesh border after transporting them by boat.
Local residents and boatmen rescued the victims and first took them to the Ulipur Upazila Health Complex, before they were transferred to Rangpur Medical College Hospital.
Surgeons at Rangpur Medical College Hospital have successfully performed operations to remove bullet splinters from both men.
One of the victims remains in critical condition with multiple lacerated injuries to the lumbar region and a rib fracture, according to hospital officials.
Director Brigadier General Ashikur Rahman stated that the victims are receiving free medical treatment, including all medicines and pathological tests, on humanitarian grounds.
caption:
Mistaken for Bangladeshis, two Indian citizens were beaten and shot by their own border guards.

Two Indian citizens from the South Salmara Mancachar district of Assam were shot by the Border Security Force (BSF) on Sunday night in the Ulipur border area of Kurigram.

The victims, identified as mason Ismail Hossain and Abdul Alim, were allegedly detained by BSF members inside Indian territory during a cattle smuggling operation.

Ismail Hossain reported that BSF personnel beat him with sticks and shot him after mistakenly claiming he was a Bangladeshi, despite his pleas that he was an Indian citizen.

The BSF allegedly left the victims bleeding at the zero line of the Bangladesh border after transporting them by boat.

Local residents and boatmen rescued the victims and first took them to the Ulipur Upazila Health Complex, before they were transferred to Rangpur Medical College Hospital.

Surgeons at Rangpur Medical College Hospital have successfully performed operations to remove bullet splinters from both men.

One of the victims remains in critical condition with multiple lacerated injuries to the lumbar region and a rib fracture, according to hospital officials.

Director Brigadier General Ashikur Rahman stated that the victims are receiving free medical treatment, including all medicines and pathological tests, on humanitarian grounds.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune
